preconditions.description: The number of words in Old Berland language is between 1 and 1000, inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= li <= 1000 for li in lengths)
preconditions.description: The lengths of the words are natural numbers not exceeding 1000.

postconditions.description: The output is either 'YES' or 'NO' indicating whether the words can be reconstructed.

postconditions.expression: output == 'YES' ==> all(i < j for i, j in zip(lengths, lengths[1:]))
postconditions.description: If the output is 'YES', the words can be reconstructed and are in strictly increasing order of their lengths.

postconditions.expression: output == 'YES' ==> all(not word.startswith(other) for i, word in enumerate(words) for other in words[:i])
postconditions.description: If the output is 'YES', no word is a prefix of another.
If the output is 'YES', the number of words output is equal to the number of input words.
